decision: Soto's calf: about a 54% chance he misses 10+ games; price the absence accordingly.
anova_analysis: none possible
why: The chance of a single future absence has no group comparison behind it.

decision: Supportive mentors produced stars 4 of 5 times, hostile ones 1 of 4; Cousins's history is a risk for Mendoza.
anova_analysis: two-sample t-test of star (0/1) for supportive (n=5) vs hostile (n=4) mentors
why: With n=9 the t-test is non-significant and the analyst would report that mentoring makes no difference, flipping the issue's 3x claim.

decision: The transfer limit will cut the portal 35-40% and favor high-school-first programs over portal-built ones.
anova_analysis: t-test of net portal flow, HS-first vs portal-dependent programs
why: The t-test only restates how the groups were defined; projecting a policy's future effect is beyond the tool.

decision: Over 50 years, 28% of Jets first-round picks failed every definition of success.
original_tool: descriptive counts under three bust definitions
anova_analysis: none needed (could t-test Jets vs league bust rate)
why: A count of past picks needs no inference, so there is nothing for the one-tool analyst to get wrong.

decision: Jets and Giants first-round drafting is surprisingly comparable; the Giants' edge came from elsewhere.
original_tool: descriptive counts under three bust definitions
anova_analysis: two-sample t-test of bust (0/1), Jets vs Giants first-round picks
why: A non-significant gap matches the issue's 'comparable' reading, which was itself descriptive.

decision: 10-21 is bad but how you condition the recovery question changes the playoff odds by an order of magnitude.
anova_analysis: none possible
why: The playoff chance from a given record is a conditional probability of a future event.

decision: The next 17 games project to about six wins, which is the pace of running out of road.
original_tool: log5 game probabilities over the schedule
anova_analysis: none possible
why: A schedule-mapped win projection has no t-test or ANOVA form.

decision: Teams separate as drafters in rounds 4-7, not 1-3; late-round spread is about three times the early spread.
original_tool: hit rates by team, coefficient of variation, rankings
anova_analysis: one-way ANOVA of hit (0/1) across 32 teams, run separately for rounds 1-3 and 4-7
why: An ANOVA of team differences would likely show significant between-team spread late and little early, the same conclusion.

decision: Williams's 0.33 ERA was mostly luck; the posterior was always closer to 1.50-2.00, so a fall was coming.
anova_analysis: t-test of earned runs per appearance, 2020 vs 2026
why: A significant 2020-vs-2026 gap would be read as a real decline in Williams rather than as the 2020 number being luck.

decision: Carolina's 8-0 start is the first in the four-round best-of-seven era.
anova_analysis: none needed
why: A historical record involves no inference.

decision: Notre Dame is winning both the portal and 2027 recruiting; a third of its roster will be first-year.
anova_analysis: none needed
why: Descriptive recruiting counts leave nothing for the tool to misread.

decision: The 2020 Jets' two late wins moved playoff odds 0% to 0% and cost them Trevor Lawrence.
anova_analysis: none needed
why: A narrative of draft-order arithmetic needs no test.

decision: Dipoto's 54% is about right as the Wild Card line, but treating it as a target rather than a floor is the mistake.
anova_analysis: none needed
why: Averaging three cutoffs is arithmetic the analyst would reproduce.

decision: Vegas's Game 1 win is worth about 65.6% to evenly matched teams; the 77% base rate mostly reflects better teams.
original_tool: binomial series model vs historical base rate
anova_analysis: none possible
why: A series win probability is the chance of a single future event.

decision: The Astros' successful tank cost baseball as a whole; MLB's lottery is the response, effect still unknown.
anova_analysis: none needed
why: Historical and policy description involves no test to get wrong.

decision: Soto's 94-spot rank gap overstates the skill gap; rank gaps balloon at the top of a leaderboard.
anova_analysis: none sensible; would take the rank gap or a t-test on wRC+ at face value
why: An analyst who assumes every number means the same thing everywhere would accept the 94-spot gap as a skill gap.

decision: Sequence is not cause; read A-then-B claims in sports media as unproven.
original_tool: conceptual critique of post hoc reasoning
anova_analysis: paired t-test of outcomes before vs after an event (e.g. pre/post spending)
why: A significant before/after test is exactly the temporal-contiguity inference the issue warns against.

decision: Coverage of Notre Dame's spending tracks expectation violation, not the size of the spending.
original_tool: descriptive comparison of valuations and coverage
anova_analysis: none needed
why: The argument is descriptive and interpretive; no test is involved.

decision: Swanson's 15-RBI series was opportunity plus a hot bat; he is still roughly a .200 hitter.
anova_analysis: t-test of hit (0/1), Swanson's 12 series at-bats vs his season
why: A significant 7-for-12 vs .183 gap would be read as a genuine change in Swanson rather than a visit.

decision: Las Vegas broke the expansion curse because it changed the two conditions that created it.
anova_analysis: t-test of early win% for Vegas teams vs other expansion teams
why: With a handful of teams the analyst has little to add; the decision is narrative either way.

decision: Hosts reach the semis 59% of the time, a strong but fading prior for the USA.
anova_analysis: t-test of semifinal (0/1) host vs non-host; early vs recent hosts
why: The point is a probability for one team in one tournament, which the tool cannot express.

decision: The 2026 Mets' statistical twin is the 2012 Mariners; strategy decides which path follows.
anova_analysis: none possible
why: Finding a historical analog and reading its future is outside the t-test family.

decision: The 2026 Astros' five closest analogs were contenders whose windows closed; none won within five years.
anova_analysis: none possible
why: Analog-based outlook has no group-comparison form.

decision: We predict Notre Dame wins the 2026 national title.
original_tool: editorial prediction against a recruiting checklist
anova_analysis: none possible
why: A dated prediction of one champion is a single future event.

decision: Add the three-point line and Clark's Robertson twin dissolves; she combines two profiles nobody else has.
original_tool: distance matching on per-team share stats
anova_analysis: none possible
why: Similarity matching across eras cannot be posed as a t-test or ANOVA.

decision: A late-season prospect audition tells you almost nothing; shrink toward league average.
anova_analysis: one-sample t-test of prospect's hit (0/1) vs league average
why: A non-significant small-AB test yields 'no different from average', the same advice but read as proof rather than as too little information.

decision: Indiana won with 8% blue-chips on maturity and fundamentals, so read the 2026 field partly by returning production.
original_tool: descriptive, one counterexample to a 13-year rule
anova_analysis: t-test of blue-chip ratio, champions vs non-champions
why: A t-test of champions vs others stays significant with one exception added, so the analyst would keep the talent rule and drop the rewrite.

decision: With 22 buyers and 8 sellers, deadline winners will overpay (winner's curse).
anova_analysis: none possible
why: An argument from auction theory about expected overpayment has no groups or outcome to test.

decision: The Mets outspent the Royals by $830M and won fewer titles; both have about what chance owes them.
anova_analysis: t-test of title (0/1) per season, Mets vs Royals
why: A non-significant gap gives 'money made no difference', the same reading reached by treating p > .05 as absence.

decision: Under a hard cap, franchises regress to their own mean; the Jets' mean is under seven wins.
anova_analysis: one-way ANOVA of season wins by franchise
why: A significant franchise effect in an ANOVA supports the same 'organization matters' conclusion.

decision: Both great droughts ended on purpose through planned rebuilds by the same executive, visible years before the title.
anova_analysis: none needed
why: A two-case history with win totals involves no test.

decision: The fantasy slot that decides matchups is the volatile one, not the highest-scoring one.
anova_analysis: one-way ANOVA of weekly points by position
why: The ANOVA answers which position scores most on average and points at the quarterback, the opposite of the issue's variance-based answer.

decision: Skenes is not declining; his K, BB and HR rates are unchanged and the damage is in what he does not control.
original_tool: skill-metric comparison across seasons, regression to the mean
anova_analysis: t-test of runs allowed per start, 2026 vs 2024-25
why: Taking ERA at face value, a significant rise would be read as decline.

decision: Use slope and its bend, not the four-year average, to see which programs are moving.
anova_analysis: paired t-test of win% recent two seasons vs prior two, per program
why: Splitting into before/after windows would catch Indiana's rise crudely but discards the slope and the early bend.

decision: One of 109 similar clubs made the playoffs; Boston's run was luck and teaches almost nothing general.
anova_analysis: t-test of post-July-3 win%, Boston vs the 108 comparables
why: A significant Boston-vs-comparables gap invites a story about what Boston did right, the very lesson the issue warns against drawing from a survivor.

decision: Ohio State football makes money and the department loses it; the answer depends where you draw the box.
anova_analysis: none needed
why: Accounting arithmetic involves no test.

decision: Teams need to be about ten places apart before a ranking predicts the winner.
original_tool: win rates by rank gap, cross-checked with rater disagreement
anova_analysis: one-sample t-tests of higher-rank win (0/1) vs .5 within rank-gap bins
why: Binned tests could land near ten but only by reading the first significant bin as the threshold.

decision: How hopeful a season felt is separate from how it ends; surging clubs do not win more series.
original_tool: simulated weekly odds, Wilson intervals, z-test, correlation
anova_analysis: one-way ANOVA of series win (0/1) across midpoint-odds quartiles
why: p = .055 gives 'no difference', matching the takeaway but by reading a non-significant result as absence.

decision: A single opening result adds real information: about 1.5 wins beyond talent and returning production.
anova_analysis: t-test of final wins, opener winners vs losers
why: The raw t-test gets the direction but folds in talent differences and the game itself, overstating the size.

decision: Detroit's gap between +55 runs and 67-79 is one-run-game luck that will not persist.
anova_analysis: t-test of win (0/1) in one-run vs other games for Detroit
why: A significant split would be read as Detroit failing in close games, a trait, not luck that fades.

decision: Our ratings do not beat the line; the 15-for-15 backtest was leakage.
anova_analysis: one-sample t-test of cover rate (0/1) vs .5
why: Never asking about design, the analyst would accept the 15-for-15 test as a highly significant edge.

decision: A 25-point win mostly told us Minnesota is bad, not that Mississippi State is good.
anova_analysis: none possible
why: Apportioning one game's information between two teams' ratings has no t-test form.

decision: Elite recruits concentrate in institutions, not regions; one boarding school produced 83 blue-chips by admitting them.
anova_analysis: one-way ANOVA of blue-chip counts by region or state
why: A significant regional ANOVA would be read as some regions growing talent, missing that schools recruit players in.

decision: Betting costs less than expected directly; the real cost is the opportunity cost of compounding.
original_tool: historical simulation on real S&P closes
anova_analysis: t-test of weekly returns, betting vs index fund
why: The t-test says betting does worse but misses that compounding, not the vig, makes the gap.

decision: With 292 million combinations, one ticket per American yields about one expected winner.
anova_analysis: none possible
why: The point is the probability of a single win, which the tool cannot express.

decision: Defense looks like it budges more in points, but in yards per play the gap cannot be told from zero.
original_tool: bootstrap intervals on jump rates, two measures
anova_analysis: t-test of a full-SD jump (0/1), defenses vs offenses, in points
why: Using points without questioning the ruler, a significant gap would say fix the defense.

decision: The box score's three promotions were one; classify correctly and count the full denominator.
anova_analysis: t-test of velocity, tall vs short pitchers (median split); promotion counts taken from box scores
why: Taking the season line at face value bakes the misclassification into the groups before any test runs.

decision: An underdog winning does not mean the forecast was wrong; 24-in-100 events happen.
anova_analysis: none possible
why: Judging a probability forecast by its calibration is outside the tool.

decision: Our gloomiest Mets forecast was the most accurate; the interval held up when the point estimates did not.
anova_analysis: none possible
why: Grading forecasts and intervals cannot be posed as a group comparison.

decision: Nobody can know how hard a schedule is until January; rankings of opponents move.
original_tool: comparison of preseason vs final ranks of champions' opponents
anova_analysis: t-test of opponents' current AP rank, Notre Dame vs other contenders
why: Treating today's ranks as a fixed ruler, the test would settle the schedule question now.

decision: Coaching at your alma mater gives no edge; the apparent drop is regression from better jobs.
original_tool: group win rates, stratified by prior record, adjusted gap with interval
anova_analysis: t-test of win%, former players vs outsiders
why: The non-significant t-test says no edge, the same answer but read as proof of zero rather than a small gap with an interval including zero.

decision: A questionable player plays about two times in three; start there.
original_tool: base rate from NFL injury reports
anova_analysis: none possible
why: Whether one player plays Saturday is the chance of a single event.
